objectives: Find the equation of a line in the form y − y₁ = m(x − x₁).
Find parallel and perpendicular lines and perpendicular bisectors.
Find the area of a triangle from its vertices.
reviewNotes: The determinant-style area formula for a triangle: confirm that it is expected.

blocks.title: Equations of a line
blocks.md: Through (x₁, y₁) with gradient m, and through two points:
blocks.tex: y - y_1 = m(x - x_1) \qquad m = \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}

blocks.title: Parallel and perpendicular
blocks.md: Parallel lines: m₁ = m₂. Perpendicular lines: m₁ × m₂ = −1. The **perpendicular bisector** of AB passes through the midpoint of AB with gradient the negative reciprocal of the gradient of AB.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Forgetting the absolute value in the area formula (the area is positive).
- Using the gradient of AB instead of its negative reciprocal for the bisector.
- Mixing the order of subtraction: use the same order in the numerator and the denominator.

blocks.title: Example 1: perpendicular bisector
blocks.statement: Find the equation of the perpendicular bisector of A(1, 2) and B(5, 6).
steps: So y = −x + 7. Check: it passes through (3, 4) since 4 = −3 + 7.

blocks.title: Example 2: area
blocks.statement: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (0, 0), (6, 0) and (2, 4).

lessons.title: The circle: equation, tangent and intersections
lessons.programRef: O Level Further Mathematics — Coordinate geometry (to be checked)
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)

objectives: Write the equation of a circle from its centre and radius, and find the centre and radius from the general equation.
Find the equation of a tangent at a point on a circle.
Decide whether a point is inside, on or outside a circle.
reviewNotes: Circle geometry in coordinates (centre-radius and general form): confirm the syllabus.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Equation of a circle
blocks.md: Centre (a, b), radius r, and the general form with centre (−g, −f) and r² = g² + f² − c:

blocks.title: Tangent at a point P
blocks.md:
1. Find the centre C and the gradient of the radius CP.
2. The tangent is perpendicular to CP: its gradient is the **negative reciprocal**.
3. Use y − y₁ = m(x − x₁) with P.
4. If CP is horizontal the tangent is vertical (and vice versa).

blocks.title: Position of a point
blocks.md: Compute (x − a)² + (y − b)² for the point and compare with r²: equal means **on** the circle, smaller means **inside**, larger means **outside**.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Reading the centre as (−3, 2) instead of (3, −2): the signs are changed in the **bracket form**.
- Using r instead of r² on the right-hand side.
- Giving the gradient of the radius instead of the tangent.

blocks.title: Example 1: centre and radius
blocks.statement: Find the centre and radius of $x^2 + y^2 - 6x + 4y - 12 = 0$.

blocks.title: Example 2: tangent
blocks.statement: Show that P(6, 2) lies on this circle and find the equation of the tangent at P.
steps: (6 − 3)² + (2 + 2)² = 9 + 16 = 25 = r²: P is on the circle.
Gradient of CP = (2 + 2)/(6 − 3) = 4/3, so the tangent has gradient −3/4.
